title: Life cycle of a star
examples: What is the first stage in a star's life?
How does a star become a red giant?
Can a star just fade away?

explain.say: A star begins its life inside a giant cloud of gas and dust. We call this cloud a nebula.
When enough gas collects, gravity pulls it together, forming a protostar. This is the beginning of fusion.
Once fusion starts, the star enters the main sequence. It burns hydrogen into helium steadily.
When hydrogen runs out, the star expands greatly, becoming a red giant. This happens for sun-like stars.
For smaller stars, they shed outer layers and become a white dwarf. This is a dense, cooling core.
Very massive stars end dramatically in a supernova explosion. This event can create heavy elements.

faq.q: What is the difference between a white dwarf and a neutron star?
faq.a: A white dwarf is the leftover core of a smaller star. A neutron star is the incredibly dense remnant of a much more massive star.
asks: What happens after a red giant?
What is the densest star remnant?

faq.q: Does every star go through the red giant phase?
faq.a: No, only stars with enough mass to fuse hydrogen in the first place will reach this stage. The path depends on the star's initial size.
asks: Can a star skip the red giant phase?

faq.a: A supernova occurs when a very massive star runs out of fuel and collapses violently. This explosion scatters heavy elements into space.
asks: What triggers the biggest star explosions?

faq.q: Are nebulae where stars are born or just floating gas?
faq.a: Nebulae are vast clouds of gas and dust that are often the birthplace of new stars. Gravity causes the material within them to clump together.
asks: What is the role of gas clouds in space?
Do all gas clouds become stars?

faq.q: How long does a star spend on the main sequence?
faq.a: The time spent on the main sequence depends heavily on the star's mass. More massive stars burn fuel much faster.
asks: Is the main sequence the longest stage?

facts: Stars spend most of their lives on the main sequence.
The red giant phase occurs after hydrogen fuel is depleted.
Supernovae are powerful explosions marking the end of massive stars.
A white dwarf is supported by electron degeneracy pressure.

quiz.say: A star that has exhausted its main fuel and expanded greatly is called a:
quiz.why: The red giant phase happens when the star expands after using up its core hydrogen.

wrong.0: A white dwarf is a small, dense remnant, not the expanded phase.
wrong.1: A nebula is the cloud where stars start, not the star itself.
wrong.2: A supernova is an explosion, not the stable, expanded phase.

quiz.say: What is the initial cloud of gas and dust where stars form?
quiz.why: Nebulae are the interstellar clouds that collapse under gravity to form stars.

wrong.0: A supernova is the explosive event, not the starting material.
wrong.2: A red giant is a specific, later stage in a star's life.
wrong.3: A white dwarf is the final, small core left behind.

quiz.say: If a star is very massive, what is its likely end stage?
quiz.why: Massive stars undergo gravitational collapse leading to a supernova explosion.

wrong.0: White dwarfs are typically the remnants of less massive stars.
wrong.1: The main sequence is the long, stable middle period, not the end.
wrong.2: While it passes through this, the end for very massive stars is more dramatic.
